blocks.text: Why is Biohacking Relevant for Muscle Growth?

Exercise is good for all areas of our physical health. It strengthens muscles and bones, improves mobility, and increases energy synthesis. Regular physical activity also positively affects our psychological well-being: it improves our mood, develops relationships with others, boosts confidence, and increases emotional control. Even regular walking and stretching can significantly improve the standard of living of the elderly. New research proves that any amount of physical activity is much better for our lives than no physical activity.

If you’ve never exercised before, it’s best to start small and slowly, consistently increase the load. Do not overexert yourself — this is a direct path to injury. The human body is designed for systematic addition of activity. Therefore, it is crucial to correctly assess your physical capabilities at a particular stage of the journey and listen to the body’s reactions when increasing the load.

If there is a miracle cure for better health, it is definitely exercise and sports. They will give you both immediate and long-term benefits, energize you today, and prevent the development of diseases in the future. Sport is one of the most effective, easy, and cheap biohacking for muscle tools that anyone can use to strengthen their body and mind. Your muscles are rich in mitochondria. When you exercise, mitochondria are activated. Stimulating them with physical activity is like recharging and multiplying your internal batteries.
Thanks to exercise, mitochondria develop in your muscles and all organs, especially your heart, lungs, and brain.

In addition, regular exercise accelerates the process of autophagy (cleansing the body of dead cells) and mitophagy (destruction of malfunctioning mitochondria), which renews the body’s cellular composition.

Exercise [improves brain function](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/how-to-biohack-brain-health) by activating thought processes by releasing brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which enhances neurogenesis (especially with intense exercise) and attracts mitochondria to neurons, which become a source of energy to create new neuronal connections. The more connections, the better memory, learning, and mood, and the lower the risk of dementia in old age. One study from 2020 found that just 20 minutes of physical activity at a moderate pace is enough to improve blood flow in the hippocampus. This part of the brain is responsible for memory and cognitive function, so the more blood flows to the hippocampus, the better the whole brain works. Lack of exercise causes your internal organs to go into energy-saving mode and stop working at their best. Your brain begins to age and atrophy prematurely. And exercise also [helps slow down the overall aging of the body](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/how-biohacking-can-reverse-aging).
Best Biohacking Exercises for Muscle Growth

To achieve muscle growth, it is not enough to simply lift weights or perform exercises “on autopilot.” Real muscle growth occurs as a result of microtraumas to muscle fibers that occur during intense training. After that, the body initiates recovery processes, resulting in larger, stronger, and more resilient muscles.
The key to hypertrophy is reaching muscle failure on the last repetition. This is when the maximum number of muscle fibers is activated, which triggers growth.

The best way to achieve this is through basic, multi-joint exercises with additional weight, which load several muscle groups at once and create high stress for the body — the ideal biohacking approach to effective training.
Below is an overview of the most effective exercises for each muscle group.

items: Barbell Bench PressA basic exercise that perfectly stimulates chest muscle growth. Allows you to work with heavy weights and also engages the triceps and deltoid muscles.

Tips for Workout

If your goal is to live a long life, even the recommended 150 minutes of physical activity per week reduces the risk of premature death by 31% compared to those who don’t exercise. However, this is insufficient to maintain excellent health, and they are probably right. Official recommendations are usually aimed at the majority of the population. However, you want to enjoy all the benefits of a healthy lifestyle. In that case, the U.S. Department of Health recommends the following:

items: Move more during the day and spend less time sitting: at least some physical activity is always better than none at all.

To significantly improve health, adults should get at least 150 (2 h 30 min) to 300 (5 h) min per week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise or 75 (1 h 15 min) to 150 min per week of high-intensity physical aerobic activity. It is also advisable to combine exercises of different intensities throughout the week.

For even more benefits, engage in moderate to high-intensity muscle-strengthening exercises. Work all major muscle groups at least twice a week.Discover more workout biohacking tips[here](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/fitness-and-biohacking).

blocks.text: **5 key rules for successful training:**

items: Using a foam roller (myofascial release) is a good idea! Foam rolling helps release muscle tension, improve blood flow, and prevent injuries. Use slow, controlled movements, focusing on tight or sore areas for 30–60 seconds. Avoid rolling directly on joints or bones. Best used before a workout to increase mobility or after to aid recovery.

When to train muscles: before or after the main workout? Isolated muscle activation (e.g., glute bridges before squats) can be done before your workout to enhance performance. However, intensive strength exercises targeting specific muscles are best performed during or after the main compound movements to avoid early fatigue.

Hydration during training is quite essential! Drink small sips of water throughout your workout — don’t wait until you’re thirsty. For sessions under 60 minutes, water is enough. If you train longer or sweat heavily, consider electrolyte-enriched fluids.

Proper warm-up: muscles and joints. Start with dynamic movements that mimic the exercises you’re about to do. Include mobility work for joints and activation drills for key muscles. A good warm-up lasts 5–10 minutes and gradually increases heart rate and blood flow.

Should you eat before or after a workout? It depends on your goal. If you train for strength or muscle growth, eat a balanced meal 1.5–2 hours before (with carbs and protein). If you train fasted, be sure to refuel right after with protein and carbs to support recovery and growth.

blocks.text: Nutrition for Muscle Growth

Proper nutrition for muscle gain is the foundation of healthy growth for athletes and achieving a beautiful, toned body. You cannot afford to be careless when planning your diet. Without understanding the basic rules and consuming the necessary nutrients, your workouts will not only fail to achieve your goals, but may even have the opposite effect.

The ideal option is to consult a nutritionist and develop a personalized nutrition plan. Average data is not always 100% suitable for a biohacker with a fast or slow metabolism, specific anatomy, and chronic diseases. A nutritionist takes into account many factors, not just your weight. That is why they may prescribe additional tests and examinations.
If seeing a doctor is not an option for you, learn, consult, and understand. This is the only way to achieve results in a reasonable amount of time. Here are our recommendations for you!

When gaining muscle mass, it is vital to prevent a rapid increase in fat and excessive protein breakdown. To do this, follow the basic rules and make changes not only to your diet but also to your training routine.

It is better to “destroy” carbohydrates during training. During the mass gain period, you should consume more calories. To avoid gaining fat, it’s advisable to drink high-carbohydrate shakes 1.5-2 hours before and after intense training.

Control your triglyceride intake. Excluding animal fats from your diet inevitably reduces testosterone production. At the same time, endurance and performance decline, harmful cholesterol levels rise, and vitamins and minerals are no longer absorbed. Therefore, athletes are advised to consume up to 100 g of animal triglycerides, while avoiding “harmful” and excessively fatty foods such as snacks.

Do not overdo it with cardio workouts. Otherwise, they can start to “eat away” at your muscles. To maintain normal cardiovascular function, a couple of half-hour runs per week are sufficient. The main workouts should take no more than 60 minutes. It is better to reduce the number of sets for each exercise to 5 and the number of repetitions to 12.

Balance your diet. The universal ratio of macronutrients during muscle mass gain is up to 20% fat, about 30% protein, and up to 60% carbohydrates. At the same time, fats should be polyunsaturated, and carbohydrates should be complex. Eat at least 3 meals a day, and consume carbohydrates 1.5-2 hours before and after training.
Drink enough fluids. When gaining weight, you should drink about 3 liters per day. Otherwise, you risk dehydration and slowing down muscle growth.

Another prerequisite is healthy sleep and the correct alternation of intense exercise with rest. Do not sleep less than 8 hours a day. Remember that muscle mass is gained not during training, but during rest. Special attention should be paid to stretching your muscles. If you don’t get enough sleep, their growth may not be accompanied by an increase in volume. Also, don’t forget to vary your training routine to prevent your body from getting used to the workload and to protect yourself from stress, which increases cortisol levels.
Protein-Rich Food List

Getting enough protein daily is essential for your overall health. Healthy protein sources include eggs, nuts, lean meats, fish, dairy, and certain grains. The recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for protein is set at 0.36 grams (g) of protein per pound of your body weight (0.8 g per kilogram). Remember that this reflects the minimum protein required to meet your body’s needs.
Including a variety of high-protein foods in your diet is essential for muscle growth, recovery, and overall health. Some of the top protein-rich foods include:

items: **Eggs** – a complete protein source with essential amino acids.
**Chicken breast** – lean and versatile, with about 31 g of protein per 100 g.
**Cottage cheese** – high in casein protein, which digests slowly and supports muscle repair.
**Greek yogurt** – rich in protein and probiotics; great as a snack or meal addition.
**Lean beef** – a powerful source of protein, iron, and vitamin B12.
**Fish** – tuna, salmon, and cod are excellent for both protein and healthy fats.
**Lentils & chickpeas** – ideal for plant-based diets; provide fiber and protein.
**Quinoa** – a rare plant-based complete protein containing all nine essential amino acids.
**Nuts & seeds** – almonds, peanuts, and chia seeds offer protein along with healthy fats.

blocks.text: Combining animal and plant sources ensures a broader nutrient intake and supports a more sustainable and flexible approach to nutrition.
The 8 Best Supplements for Muscle Growth

There are many biohacking products for muscle growth, and sometimes it’s difficult to find something relevant and safe. Here are some of them, which worldwide biohacking experts recommend. But please consult your doctor before using any of them!
1. Whey Protein Powder

Whey is the liquid left after milk is curdled and strained. It’s a fast-absorbing protein, ideal for post-workout recovery. There are two main types: concentrate (higher in carbs and fat) and isolate (more refined for higher protein content and faster absorption). Since whey is derived from milk, it’s naturally found in dairy. It provides all essential amino acids for muscle growth as a complete protein. Beyond muscle benefits, whey can improve sleep and boost the immune system. Studies show that consuming 20-40g of whey daily for 8-12 weeks enhances lean muscle, strength, and [fat loss](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-for-weight-loss). For optimal results, take 20-40g within 2 hours post-exercise or every 3-4 hours if not getting enough protein from food.

2. Creatine

Creatine is a non-essential amino acid mainly stored in our muscles, and a small amount is stored in the brain. It’s naturally found in foods such as red meats and fish. In a normal diet that contains about 1-2 grams of creatine per day, muscle stores are only about 60-80% saturated. Vegans/vegetarians will likely have lower stores since natural sources mainly exist in animal meats. Creatine is one of the most widely studied supplements — namely for its ability to increase muscle mass!
3. Amino Acids

Essential amino acids are nine amino acids that must be consumed via diet because the body cannot produce them on its own. Therefore, you can obtain essential amino acids naturally from any animal-based product! Essential amino acids are used in muscle/protein metabolism and have been postulated to help promote increases in lean body mass. Supplementing with essential amino acids in fasted states or low-calorie diets can preserve lean tissue and stimulate muscle protein synthesis. There is no limit on the number of essential amino acids you can consume daily. Regarding frequency, doses of 5-9g of such amino acids are recommended before and/or following resistance exercise to stimulate muscle protein synthesis.
4. Carnitine

L-carnitine is naturally produced by the liver and kidneys and plays a major role in lipid metabolism. Namely, it helps facilitate the transport of fatty acids into the mitochondria of the cell so they can be metabolized. However, it also plays minor roles in pathways that regulate muscle protein metabolism and can act as an antioxidant. While this supplement still warrants further research, it is recommended that it should be taken with carbohydrates to increase bioavailability and that ingesting 2-3g/day for at least 3 months can prevent exercise-induced muscle damage.

Sleep and recovery

[Adjusting your sleep patterns](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-sleep) is an integral part of biohacking. Getting a good night’s rest is essential for normal body and cognitive function. Quality sleep improves memory, attention, and learning ability. A good night’s rest reduces irritability and [increases stress tolerance](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-for-stress-management-what-about-mental-health). Sleep deprivation and insomnia are associated with an increased risk of depression and anxiety disorders.
Biohacking recovery methods
Effective recovery is the key to progress in training. Among the most effective biohacking methods are:

items: Cryotherapy – brief exposure to extreme cold stimulates circulation, reduces inflammation, and accelerates muscle recovery.
Saunas – thermal stress improves blood circulation, increases endurance, and promotes the elimination of toxins.
Vibration therapy – stimulates muscles and fascia, reduces tension, and accelerates tissue regeneration.

blocks.text: Incorporating these practices into your routine allows you to train harder and recover smarter.
Advanced Biohacking Methods

In the world of biohacking, more and more methods are emerging to optimize training and accelerate results. Here are three advanced techniques that can improve endurance, concentration, and muscle growth — if used correctly:

items: Blood Flow Restriction (BFR) promotes muscle growth at lower loads. To avoid the risk of thrombosis, it is recommended to use it under the supervision of specialists.
Nootropics — increase concentration and motivation. Popular options: L-tyrosine, caffeine, rhodiola. It is essential to take the correct dosage to avoid overloading the nervous system.
Microdosing — can improve endurance and recovery if used in countries where it is legal. It is essential to follow proven protocols and consult with specialists.

Common Mistakes in Muscle Growth Biohacking

It’s hard to get overtrained during moderate-intensity exercise. Remember the most essential thing: exercise is stressful. To become hormetic, stress must be impermanent, not excessive, and after it should always be recovered; otherwise, it will simply destroy your body. The maximum allowable amount of intense training per week is six days of one hour each. If you squeeze the maximum out of yourself all seven days in a row, it will have a negative impact.
